Lemma
[strict positivity of the second time-derivative at $q=p$]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-4-1-posdef ↗ lem:dc-ch3-2-9-c2diffeo

1. ch3:4.1At $q=p$ one has $\exp _p^{-1}(p)=0$, so the $\langle u'',u angle _p$ term of $G(p,v)$ vanishes and $G(p,v)=2 ig|D(\exp _p^{-1})_0(w) ig|_p^2$. Since $D(\exp _p^{-1})_0$ is a linear isomorphism and $\langle \cdot ,\cdot angle _p$ is positive definite, $G(p,v)>0$ for $v eq 0$.
Proof

\sketch

$u(0,p,v)=\exp _p^{-1}(p)=0$ kills the first term. The derivative $D(\exp _p^{-1})_0$ is the inverse of $D(\varphi _p\circ \exp _p)_0$ (inverse function theorem), hence injective, so $D(\exp _p^{-1})_0(w) eq 0$ for $w eq 0$; then $ ig|D(\exp _p^{-1})_0(w) ig|_p^2>0$ by positive definiteness of the metric at $p$ (section 3).

□
